title: Delivery fee before lunch
scenario: You are waiting for limited-edition sneakers when a text says the courier cannot deliver without a $2.18 address fee paid before noon. The message arrives on the expected delivery day.

answers.A: Ask a parent or trusted adult to help verify the carrier and tracking number.
answers.B: Pay the tiny fee because the timing matches the delivery perfectly.
answers.C: Check the order and carrier tracking in the retailer/carrier app or website you open yourself.

explanation: Scammers rely on the huge number of people expecting packages. Small fees can collect card and personal data.
proTip: Expected package, unexpected link: still verify.
